predecessors.name: Bamana Empire
predecessors.text: Djenné and Massina, the Inner Niger Delta around Mopti, where Hamdullahi stood

successors.name: Tukulor Empire
successors.text: The Cliopatria 1861 outline without the Bambara remnant at Ségou

ledger.x: 1818: Seku Amadu founds the Massina Empire.

The rest of Cliopatria's 1822 outline (Fakala-Kunari, Hayre-Seno, Nabbe-Dude and the Niger bend) is undated on the pages: the Massina page names five regions without years, the Seku Amadu page says the empire extended to the Inner Niger Delta and exerted some authority over Timbuktu, Ségou and Kaarta.
ledger.cp: Dogon, Fulbe and Tuareg lands (no dossier)

wars.name: Fulani jihad of Massina
wars.outcome: Seku Amadu defeats the Bambara and takes Djenné and the Mopti country in 1818; the Massina page says a force of 1,000 routed a 100,000-strong army under General Jamogo Seri at Noukouma (no year on that page).

wars.name: Massina-Timbuktu wars
wars.outcome: Massina conquers Timbuktu in 1826/7 and holds it firmly from 1833; the Tuareg drove off the garrison in 1840, lose in 1841, drive Massina out in 1842-1844; Massina starves the city back by 1846.

wars.name: Umar Tall's conquest of Massina
wars.outcome: Umar Tall attacks in 1862, wins at Cayawal and enters Hamdullahi on 16 May, levelling it; Amadu III is captured and put to death.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Massina frontier; the Djenné-Mopti heartland is known by its towns, the Seno, Niger bend and Segu edges are approximate.
